issues.finding: An arbitrary replacement term may contain a variable bound by a quantifier in the proof; literal replacement would capture it.
issues.proposed_resolution: Specify capture-avoiding substitution and choose bound variables fresh for the replacement term before applying the displayed rule transformations.

issues.finding: Contexts are multisets, but the ordinary set comprehension could erase repeated formula occurrences.
issues.proposed_resolution: Explicitly interpret this comprehension as a multiset comprehension, preserving one substituted occurrence for each original occurrence.

issues.finding: Both original and substituted universal-left diagrams are labelled universal-right.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use universal-left labels in those two diagrams only.

issues.finding: The concluding eigenparameter argument has interleaved clauses and no grammatical statement of preservation.
issues.proposed_resolution: State eigenparameter preservation using the term-disjointness assumption, then explain why the new end-sequent has no eigenparameter and the proof remains regular.

issues.finding: A highest inference can already be clean, so choosing it need not reduce the dirty count. A highest dirty inference may have clean eigenparameter rules above it, and renaming can clean other dirty rules as well, so the claimed exact n-1 count is too strong.
issues.proposed_resolution: Choose a highest dirty inference, justify regularity of its higher clean subproof, use a globally fresh parameter and strong induction on a strictly decreasing dirty count.

issues.finding: The adjacent rules-proofs section requires closed terms for quantifier instances. Replacing a constant by an open term could turn an allowed closed instance into a forbidden open one.
issues.proposed_resolution: Require the replacement term to be closed, as well as free of eigenparameters. Capture avoidance and multiplicity preservation remain stated, and the renaming application already uses closed constants.
